$comment: AGREEMENT TABLE — 'is this event addressed at the OPERATOR?' — consumed by BOTH implementations.
AUDIT FINDING 2 is the reason this file exists. `comms_search` was implemented in two languages;
I fixed the stdio renderer, believed I was done, and found the SSE copy afterwards. The reviewer's
recommendation, which has now worked three times in this repo, is an agreement test rather than
consolidation. The rule that follows: when a predicate must exist in two languages, the CASES live
in one file and both sides are asserted against it.
`shared` cases must produce the same answer on both sides. `allowedDifferences` must NOT: they
record where the two sides legitimately disagree, each with the reason. A case may only live
there if the disagreement comes from different AUTHORITY, never from drift.

shared.name: direct message addressed to the operator
direct message between two agents is fleet chatter
operator among several recipients still counts
recipient casing must not decide it
a single string recipient, not a list
channel the operator has NOT joined
an unknown event type notifies nothing

allowedDifferences.name: server_authoritative_joined_channel_vs_browser_unknown_membership
reason: Membership is UNKNOWN to the caller here. The browser must fail closed: the dashboard can see
every channel, not only the ones it joined, and its channel list loads asynchronously — so
notifying-when-unsure fires on everything for the first seconds after every reload, which is the
volume failure the whole feature is shaped around.
The server has no such window. It reads channel_members directly at the send site, so it is never
unsure; `channelJoined: null` on the server side means 'ask the database', and for this case the
This is different AUTHORITY, not disagreement. Asserting identical output here would force the
server to discard information it actually has.
